task_cmo.answer: Brief Builder helps the agency turn scattered client documents into a Greek and English briefing draft, with sources, disagreements and unanswered questions visible. For me, it makes corrections easier to trace and shows what still needs my decision. This synthetic run produced cited drafts, surfaced three conflicts and passed 17 defined checks. It did not prove time savings, reliable Greek quality or readiness for client delivery; creative drafts still contained errors. People confirm client intent, settle disagreements, review wording, sign off and judge creative claims. I would support a conditional pilot, with costs and data terms settled before starting and live use dependent on measured results.
missing: No essential information was missing for this explanation. Actual savings, total operating cost and the Greek-quality release threshold remain explicitly unproven or unresolved.
confusions: “Static review pages support command-line operation” leaves me unsure how I would actually review or correct a brief.
“Harness-only use is a policy restriction.” I cannot interpret this without technical knowledge.
“The <30-minute review target needs definition agreement: PRD §7 measures time-to-first-draft attention.” This makes the review target on sheet 10 feel unsettled.
fixes: Replace “Static review pages support command-line operation; the signature controls the handover.” with “An AI specialist runs the tool. The account lead reviews the pages and records corrections and approval before creative drafting begins.”
Replace “Harness-only use is a policy restriction.” with “Rules prohibit the drafting AI from using the answer key, but access is not technically blocked.”

Replace “The <30-minute review target needs definition agreement: PRD §7 measures time-to-first-draft attention.” with “Before the pilot, the sponsor must settle which work counts toward the 30-minute target.”
Replace “0.98 M tokens” on sheet 01 with “Usage measured; subscription capacity still unconfirmed”, keeping the detailed counts on sheet 10.

task_cfo.answer: Stage one: Haiku 4.5 533,641 + Sonnet 5 451,179 = 984,820 tokens. Creative adds Sonnet 86,441 + Opus 4.8 63,473 = 1,134,734 total. Validate assumptions in week 1. Approve four weeks, two leads×three retrospectives, S0–S1, agency workspace; creative stays shadow. Before starting: remeasure routing, confirm capacity/terms, approve costs/ceiling and Greek threshold. Week-4 release requires >80% useful questions, >70% unchanged text, <30-minute reviews, Greek threshold, both leads’ voluntary reuse, and sponsor decision. Month-2 default requires successful report/separate approval.
missing: Actual setup, training, subscription, maintenance and support costs; approved spending ceiling; confirmed subscription capacity and workspace terms. These are explicitly deferred prerequisites, so net savings cannot yet be calculated.
A full-run usage/time baseline under the changed routing, measured assembly/review effort, an agreed attention-time definition and a Greek release threshold.
confusions: “about 16 M with one creative draft each” does not identify the model; either displayed arm rounds to approximately 16M.

“Attention definitions require sponsor agreement: PRD §7 concerns time to first draft, while the review target here is <30 minutes.” The page discloses the mismatch, but the measurement definition remains unsettled.
“all three inputs are validated in week 1” leaves the separately stated, unvalidated 50-minute attention target less clearly covered.
fixes: Replace “about 16 M with one creative draft each” with “15.72M with one Opus draft per brief, or 16.07M with one Sonnet draft, at 15 briefs monthly under graded routing.”

Replace “all three inputs are validated in week 1” with “Validate baseline, volume and hourly rate in week 1; measure assembly and review time during the retrospective to test the 50-minute attention target.”
Replace “Attention definitions require sponsor agreement” with “Before week 1, the sponsor must define assembly time, review time and time to first draft, and approve how each is measured.”

task_creative.answer: (a) Signed-off evidence: audience 25–40 urban professionals; launch 15 September 2026; production budget “in the eighties,” excluding media, with total unconfirmed. Zero sugar is permitted; natural ingredients needs an approved list. (b) Hypotheses: both propositions, audience psychology, everyday ritual and visual concept—not research or agreed client lines. (c) Strike unsupported “Greek-made,” €80–85k conversion and mistaken dance retraction; judge guilt wording against the health-claim ban, verify references, record A/B/neither, and resolve six blockers. This approves evaluation only: v1 creative cannot leave shadow. (d) Specs are table lookups from a provisional stub. Code checks normalized dimensions and some ratios; it guarantees neither durations, file types, deliverable fit nor production readiness.
missing: The creative reviewer and decision date remain unassigned.
Full creative drafts and further spec rows are not embedded, limiting independent verification.
A complete creative-delivery authorization process beyond v1 is not specified.
confusions: “Owner and decision date remain unassigned.” versus “the named creative lead records a choice and corrections before week 4”: a deadline is supplied, but assignment status is unclear.
“A creative team cannot start without” is ambiguous when the sheet already presents shadow creative; it should specify production or delivery.
fixes: Replace “Owner and decision date remain unassigned.” with “Creative lead unassigned; shadow evaluation due before week 4; exact review date unset.”
Replace “A creative team cannot start without — still open, carried from the brief” with “Resolve before production or delivery; shadow exploration may continue.”
Replace “Spec (from the table, not generated)” with “Provisional table value — traffic confirmation required”.

task_engineer.answer: This run passed 17 checks on one synthetic project; it does not guarantee general completeness, supported claims or natural Greek. Models classify, flag fidelity, extract/verify, synthesize and render client/creative briefs. Code checks readiness, schemas, exact anchors, citation tags, glossary, sensitivity and limited specs; it assembles conflict candidates, while synthesis identifies contradictions. Checks miss semantic errors, duplicate/uncited questions and some spec errors. The account lead manually records resolutions and signoff in brief.json; brief_review.html displays them, toggles languages and copies questions, but saves nothing. Sign-off gates shadow creative; nothing is delivered automatically. Before week 1, the operator must rerun Sonnet extraction plus verifier, remeasure tokens/time and update subscription capacity planning; old totals are not current.
confusions: “Promise: a client brief in Greek and English, every claim with its receipt, every gap a question, nothing sent without a signature.” This sounds universal; later limitations narrow what is actually checked.
“Nothing moves past the draft without an account lead.” The precise enforced boundary appears later: entry into shadow creative requires signoff.status to equal signed_off.
fixes: Replace “Promise: a client brief in Greek and English, every claim with its receipt, every gap a question, nothing sent without a signature.” with “Target: cited Greek and English briefs with gaps surfaced as questions. Checks verify defined properties; people judge support and completeness. Sign-off gates shadow creative; v1 does not send work.”
Replace “Nothing moves past the draft without an account lead.” with “The creative stage refuses to start until the account lead records sign-off in brief.json.”
Replace “Six AI steps, two plain-code steps, one person.” with “The diagram groups six AI steps, two code steps and human sign-off; current extraction also includes a verifier agent.”
